# Automatic leading with shifted inline content

Original OOXML control generated by `tools/shifted_inline_leading_fixture.py`.
The only image is an original solid red PNG. Each of 28 pages places text and a
72pt inline picture in a vertically centered 216pt table cell. Seven text/image
shift combinations (0, +30pt and -30pt) cross four automatic line multiples
(0.8, 1, 1.2 and 2). Arial 12pt and compatibility mode 15 are explicit.

The reference application uses the unshifted font height for additional automatic leading.
It does not multiply the raised/lowered allocation box by the spacing factor.
For compression below one line, the baseline's spacing share is that font
height minus the full line descent, including a lowered picture's descent.
This share can be negative. Natural image/text extents still include the
declared shifts, and single spacing remains unchanged.

ECMA-376 Part 1 sections 17.3.1.33 (spacing), 17.3.2.24 (position), and 20.4.2.8
(inline) supply the declarations; this control records the reference application's additional
mixed-content layout behavior. No source-specific offsets are used.

The native recorder binds text origins and image bounds to source/PDF hashes.
The generator reproduces every OPC part. Browser coverage checks both native
geometry and painted image boundaries through editing, exact undo, package
preservation and export/reopen. Existing inline-object, baseline-shift and
minimum/exact-spacing controls remain the regression checks for other modes.
